chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who stipulates a condition during Hajj. How does he stipulate? He said: He says when he intends to enter the state of Ihram: 'Release me from my obligation where you detain me, and if you detain me, then it is Umrah.' I said to him: 'Then is Haj obligatory upon him next year?' He said: 'Yes.' And Safwan said: 'Several of our companions have narrated this narration, all of them say: Indeed, Haj is obligatory upon him next year.'

key_terms.مِنْ قَابِلٍ: from the following year / next year
key_terms.يُحْرِمُ: to enter the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim stipulates release from Haj if detained?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Istibsar clarifies the ruling of *shart al-habs* (stipulating release if detained), where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that if the pilgrim is indeed detained, the Umrah suffices for that year, but the Haj obligation remains pending for the following year. The narration highlights the consensus (*ijma'*) of the Shia companions, as reported by Safwan, affirming that the missed Haj must be made up in the subsequent year, establishing a clear precedent for conditional vows in Hajj jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the flexibility within Shia fiqh to accommodate unforeseen impediments while maintaining the integrity of the obligatory pilgrimage.
